findings.area: Fetch API Not Using PolymarketAPI Class
findings.problem: fetchActiveMarkets() calls fetch() directly bypassing the PolymarketAPI class which has retry logic, rate limiting, caching, and schema validation.
findings.solution: Replace raw fetch() with this.api.getMarkets() to get retry/ratelimit/cache for free.
findings.code_hint: Use: const markets = await this.api.getMarkets({ closed: false, limit: 50 })

findings.problem: analyzeMarket() has no access to price HISTORY. It only sees the current snapshot. Cannot detect momentum, mean-reversion, or trend. Trading blind on price direction.
findings.solution: Use PolymarketAPI.getPriceHistory() to fetch 24h/7d price data and compute momentum signals: SMA crossover, RSI, price change velocity.
findings.code_hint: Add: const history = await this.api.getPriceHistory(tokenId, { interval: 'hour' })

findings.problem: The bot never checks the orderbook. It doesn't know bid/ask spread, order depth, or slippage risk. It trades at 'outcomePrices' which is just the midpoint.
findings.solution: Use PolymarketAPI.getOrderbook() to check spread. Skip markets with spread > 5%. Use actual bid/ask for entry/exit pricing instead of midpoint.
findings.code_hint: Add: const book = await this.api.getOrderbook(tokenId); const spread = (bestAsk - bestBid) / bestBid * 100

findings.problem: SentimentAnalyzer is imported/available but never called in trading decisions. The bot ignores all sentiment signals despite having a full implementation.
findings.solution: Integrate sentiment into analyzeMarket() confidence scoring: fetch recent market-related text, run through SentimentAnalyzer.generateSentimentSignal(), boost/penalize confidence by ±10% based on signal.
findings.code_hint: const sentimentSignal = this.sentimentAnalyzer.generateSentimentSignal(current, history)

findings.problem: LeaderboardAnalyzer is instantiated but never called. The bot doesn't learn from top traders' positions or strategies.
findings.solution: Use leaderboard data to identify which markets top traders are active in. Add a 'smart money' factor to confidence: if top traders have positions in a market, boost confidence by 15-20%.
findings.code_hint: const topTraders = await this.analyzer.getTopTradersByWinRate('week', 10)

findings.area: Only BUYs, Never Direct SELLs on New Markets
findings.problem: analyzeMarket() only returns side='BUY'. The bot can never short/sell a new market. For prediction markets, selling 'Yes' at 0.85 can be as profitable as buying 'Yes' at 0.15.
findings.solution: Add contrarian logic: if a market is overpriced (> 0.75) and momentum is declining, generate a SELL signal for the Yes side (equivalent to buying No).
findings.code_hint: if (price > 0.75 && momentumDecline) { side = 'SELL'; outcomeIndex = 0; }

findings.problem: checkExitSignals() always exits the FULL position. No scaling out. If a position hits +8%, selling half and letting the rest run to +12% is better.
findings.solution: Implement tiered exits: sell 50% at targetProfit/2, sell remaining at full target. This locks in profits while maintaining upside.
findings.code_hint: const sellQty = pnlPercent >= CONFIG.targetProfitPercent ? position.quantity : Math.floor(position.quantity / 2)

findings.problem: fetchActiveMarkets() only fetches limit=50. Polymarket has 500+ active markets. The bot is only seeing ~10% of available opportunities.
findings.solution: Increase limit to 200+ or implement pagination. Also add sorting by volume DESC to get the best markets first.
findings.code_hint: fetch('...?closed=false&limit=200&order=volume&ascending=false')

findings.problem: The bot treats all markets equally. Sports, politics, crypto, economics all have different dynamics. No category awareness for diversification.
findings.solution: Use PolymarketAPI.getTags() to categorize markets. Enforce max 2-3 positions per category. Different strategies per category (sports = higher confidence needed).
findings.code_hint: const tags = await this.api.getTags(); // categorize by tag

findings.area: Resume Loses Peak Price / Trailing Stop Data
findings.problem: When resuming from saved state, marketPriceCache is empty. All trailing stop peak prices are lost. Positions that were near trailing stop will reset.
findings.solution: Save and restore marketPriceCache in the JSON report file.
findings.code_hint: Add 'peakPrices' field to report JSON and restore on resume

findings.problem: No risk-adjusted return metric in reports. Raw return % doesn't account for volatility. Need Sharpe ratio for proper strategy evaluation.
findings.solution: Track portfolio value each cycle, compute returns series, calculate Sharpe = mean(returns) / std(returns) * sqrt(annualization_factor).
findings.code_hint: const returns = portfolioHistory.map((v,i) => i > 0 ? (v-prev)/prev : 0)

findings.problem: Buys/sells execute at exact price with zero slippage. Real markets have 0.5-3% slippage depending on order size and liquidity.
findings.solution: Add slippage model: slippage = baseFee + (orderSize / liquidity) * impactFactor. Apply to execution price. Makes simulation more realistic.
findings.code_hint: const slippage = 0.001 + (totalValue / liquidity) * 0.05; const adjustedPrice = side === 'BUY' ? price * (1 + slippage) : price * (1 - slippage)

findings.problem: Flat 0.1% fee doesn't match Polymarket's actual fee structure. Real fees are tiered and depend on whether you're maker/taker.
findings.solution: Model Polymarket's actual fee structure: makers get 0% fees (or rebates), takers pay 1-2% depending on the market.
findings.code_hint: const fees = isMaker ? 0 : totalValue * 0.015

findings.problem: Every call to updatePortfolioHistory() appends to the array. Over 7 days with 5-minute cycles = 2,016 entries. Not huge, but no pruning.
findings.solution: Keep only last N entries (e.g., 1000) or downsample older entries to hourly.
findings.code_hint: if (this.portfolioValueHistory.length > 2000) { this.portfolioValueHistory = this.portfolioValueHistory.slice(-1000); }

findings.problem: getMetrics() doesn't calculate profit factor (gross wins / gross losses). This is a key metric for evaluating strategy quality.
findings.solution: Add: profitFactor = totalWins > 0 && totalLosses > 0 ? totalWins / totalLosses : 0
findings.code_hint: profitFactor: wins.reduce((a,b) => a+b, 0) / Math.abs(losses.reduce((a,b) => a+b, 0))

findings.problem: When restoring positions, createdAt is set to new Date(). This breaks time-based exits because restored positions appear brand new.
findings.solution: Save createdAt in the report JSON and restore it properly.
findings.code_hint: createdAt: pos.createdAt ? new Date(pos.createdAt) : new Date()

findings.problem: The PolymarketAPI class has retry, caching, rate limiting, and validation. But week-test.ts calls raw fetch() directly, getting none of these benefits.
findings.solution: This is the single biggest integration gap. Connect week-test to use this.api.getMarkets() instead of raw fetch().
findings.code_hint: Replace fetchActiveMarkets body with: return this.api.getMarkets({...})

findings.area: Cache Key Includes Full Options Object
findings.problem: Cache key = url + JSON.stringify(options). If options change slightly (e.g., different header order), cache misses even for same request.
findings.solution: Normalize cache key: sort options keys, exclude volatile headers.
findings.code_hint: const cacheKey = `${url}_${sortedParams}`

findings.problem: If two callers request the same market simultaneously, both make API calls. Should deduplicate in-flight requests.
findings.solution: Use a Map of pending Promises. If a request for the same URL is already in-flight, return the existing Promise instead of making a new request.
findings.code_hint: private pendingRequests: Map<string, Promise<any>> = new Map()

findings.problem: AbortController timeout is hardcoded to 30000ms. Different endpoints may need different timeouts.
findings.solution: Make timeout configurable per-request or by endpoint type.
findings.code_hint: const timeout = options.timeout || 30000

findings.problem: SentimentAnalyzer exists with full analysis capability but has NO data source. No Twitter/Reddit/news API integration. It's a dead module.
findings.solution: Integrate a free news API (e.g., NewsAPI, Google News RSS) to fetch real headlines related to market questions. Parse and feed to analyzeSentiment().
findings.code_hint: const headlines = await fetchNewsForMarket(market.question); const sentimentData = headlines.map(h => ({ source: 'news', text: h, ... }))

findings.problem: Only 18 positive and 18 negative words. Prediction-market-specific vocabulary is missing (e.g., 'likely', 'unlikely', 'confirmed', 'denied', 'postponed').
findings.solution: Expand word lists with prediction-market and political vocabulary. Add domain-specific terms: 'confirmed', 'denied', 'postponed', 'canceled', 'likely', 'unlikely'.
findings.code_hint: Add: 'confirmed', 'approved', 'passed', 'likely', 'certain' to positive; 'denied', 'rejected', 'postponed', 'unlikely', 'canceled' to negative

findings.problem: Tokenizer only checks single words. 'not good' requires looking back one position. More complex phrases like 'better than expected' aren't captured.
findings.solution: Add bigram detection for common phrases: 'better than', 'worse than', 'more likely', 'less likely', 'highly unlikely'.
findings.code_hint: Check 2-word and 3-word phrases before falling back to single words

findings.problem: Full implementation for tracking top traders but never called from week-test. Wasted capability that could provide a 'smart money' signal.
findings.solution: In runCycle(), periodically (every 6 hours?) fetch top trader positions. If top traders are active in a market, boost that market's confidence score.
findings.code_hint: if (cycle % 72 === 0) { topTraderMarkets = await this.analyzer... }

findings.problem: KNOWN_TOP_TRADERS has only 2 addresses, one of which is clearly fake (0x8d8f3f5c...). Not enough data to derive meaningful signals.
findings.solution: Implement trader discovery: fetch recent high-volume trades from the data API, identify wallets with consistent wins, add them to the tracking list.
findings.code_hint: Discover traders from: data-api.polymarket.com/activity?limit=500

findings.area: No Caching of Individual Trader Metrics
findings.problem: calculateTraderMetrics() fetches fresh data every call. With multiple traders, this means many API calls per cycle.
findings.solution: Cache individual trader metrics with 30-minute TTL.
findings.code_hint: private traderMetricsCache: Map<string, { data: TraderMetrics; fetchedAt: number }>

findings.problem: Dashboard polls /api/status periodically. With 5-minute cycles, this is fine but not real-time. WebSocket would push updates instantly.
findings.solution: Add WebSocket (ws library) or Server-Sent Events for push-based updates.
findings.code_hint: import { WebSocketServer } from 'ws'; // push report data on each cycle

findings.problem: Only serves current snapshot. No endpoint for historical portfolio value, trade history over time, or performance charts.
findings.solution: Add /api/history endpoint that returns portfolioValueHistory from simulator. Store historical reports in a ring buffer or file.
findings.code_hint: app.get('/api/history', (req, res) => { ... })

findings.problem: Dashboard and API endpoints are completely open. Anyone can access trading data.
findings.solution: Add basic auth or JWT token for dashboard access.
findings.code_hint: Use env-config.ts security.jwtSecret for token validation

findings.problem: getCache() returns ThreadSafeCache<string> but callers store arbitrary objects. The generic types don't flow correctly through the singleton.
findings.solution: Make getCache() generic or use ThreadSafeCache<string, any>.
findings.code_hint: export function getCache<V = any>(): ThreadSafeCache<string, V>

findings.problem: No tracking of hit rate, miss rate, eviction count. Can't diagnose caching effectiveness.
findings.solution: Add hitCount, missCount, evictionCount counters. Expose via getStats().
findings.code_hint: getStats() should return: { hitRate, missRate, evictionCount }

findings.problem: Can only test strategy by running live for 7 days. No way to replay historical data to validate strategy changes before deployment.
findings.solution: Build a backtesting mode that replays saved market snapshots through the strategy engine. Run 100 simulated weeks in minutes instead of 1 real week.
findings.code_hint: class Backtester { async run(historicalData: MarketSnapshot[]) { ... } }

findings.problem: Trading logic is hardcoded in week-test.ts. Can't swap strategies, A/B test, or compose multiple signals without rewriting the whole file.
findings.solution: Extract strategy into a Strategy interface: { analyze(market): Signal, shouldExit(position): boolean }. Allow pluggable strategies.
findings.code_hint: interface Strategy { analyze(market: MarketData): TradeSignal; shouldExit(position: VirtualPosition, market: MarketData): ExitSignal; }

findings.problem: Trade history lives in memory. On restart, all history is lost. Only the latest snapshot survives in test-results.json.
findings.solution: Append each trade to a trades.jsonl (JSON Lines) file for full audit trail. This enables post-hoc analysis without losing data on restart.
findings.code_hint: fs.appendFileSync('trades.jsonl', JSON.stringify(trade) + '\n')

findings.problem: Everything runs on a fixed 5-minute timer. If a market moves 20% in 1 minute, the bot doesn't react until the next cycle.
findings.solution: Consider WebSocket connection to Polymarket for real-time price updates. React to significant price movements immediately.
findings.code_hint: Use Polymarket WebSocket API for live price streams
